name: one-action-common-state-v1
question: What are the immediate and future consequences of one HOLD, BRAKE or PUSH from the same complete training state?
host_policy: unchanged learned Architect, examples/chuck-loss-architect.json, seed overridden by run seed
window_stream: SplitMix64 from run seed, modulo train_tokens-context; same as v1
split: first 90 percent training, last 10 percent held out
metrics: immediate loss before and after intervention on its own window
mean loss on the four fixed future probe windows after each horizon
mean loss on the eight fixed held-out windows after each horizon
comparison: For each separate metric, HOLD loss minus action loss. Winners use exact recorded F32 loss equality; all ties retained.
host_noninterference: Independent no-probe and probe processes must match all 512 host-step losses, actions, policy identities and complete body/tape/optimizer/RNG identities, plus final saved body, moments, controls and policy bytes.
snapshot: CPU-only deep copy of every tape output and gradient, tape operation metadata, body parameters with restored parameter aliases, Adam m/v/acc_grad and counters, global and all per-slot Chuck state, complete Architect life, Chuck noise RNG, window RNG, and train/eval mode.
rng_scope: These bodies consume the notorch initialization RNG only during body_init; all branch operations are deterministic apart from the separately saved Chuck noise stream.
negative_gate: Suppressing parameter restoration in a scratch build must fail snapshot_restore_exact.
failure_receipt_gate: A post-action NaN injected in a scratch v1 runner must receive reward -1, preserve a strict JSON failure receipt and final policy/body/optimizer artifacts, and stop before another step.
